chunks: 1. Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqah, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, that he said:

A person in janabah should not touch a dirham or dinar upon which the Name of Allah is written, nor perform istinja' while wearing a ring in which the Name of Allah is inscribed, nor have intercourse while it is upon him, nor enter the place of relieving oneself while it is upon him.

2. As for what Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Barqi, from Wahb ibn Wahb, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said: The inscription on the ring of my father was: 'All might belongs to Allah altogether,' and it was on his left hand and he would perform istinja' with it; and the inscription on the ring of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام was: 'The dominion belongs to Allah,' and it was on his left hand and he would perform istinja' with it. This report is to be understood as taqiyyah, because its narrator is Wahb ibn Wahb, and he is an 'Ammi, weak, and abandoned in hadith in that which he alone reports. Furthermore, what we have presented belongs to the etiquettes of taharah and is not among its obligations. That which indicates this is:
3. What Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Qasim, from Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man wants to go to relieve himself while he is wearing a ring in which the Name of Allah, Exalted is He, is inscribed? He said: I do not like that. He said: Then if it contains the name of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم? He said: There is no problem.

key_terms.اسْمُ اللَّهِ: the Name of Allah inscribed on an object
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: a person in the state of janabah
key_terms.خَاتَمٌ: a ring worn on the hand
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem; it is unobjectionable
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: performs istinja', cleansing oneself after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing a ring inscribed with the Name of Allah when entering the toilet or performing istinja'?
ai.summary: This report discusses the etiquette of ritual purity concerning items bearing the Name of Allah, especially rings and coins. It indicates dislike for entering the place of relieving oneself or performing istinja' while wearing such an item, while also clarifying through the later discussion that this falls under etiquette rather than strict obligation.
